  {
    "text": "The Data Center sandbox is a working example of design-driven automation for data center fabrics. You describe a new data center by choosing a design template and a location, and Infrahub generates its devices, interfaces, cabling, IP addresses and device configurations. It is set up for teams that build spine-leaf fabrics and want every new data center built from the same standard designs."

## What's in the sandbox

<SandboxBlocks blocks={[
  {
    "p": [
      {
        "text": "The sandbox contains example locations, providers and data center designs for Arista, Cisco, Juniper and SONiC devices. It also has a "
      },
      {
        "text": "service portal",
        "href": "https://portal-demo-dc.opsmill.app"
      },
      {
        "text": " where you request a new data center by filling in a form, and view the racks of existing data centers."
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "p": [
      {
        "text": "The demo follows "
      },
      {
        "text": "design-driven automation",
        "href": "/demo-dc/concepts#design-driven-automation"
      },
      {
        "text": ": you describe a data center as a design, such as a number of spines and leaf switches, and a Generator creates the devices, interfaces, links and IP addresses that the design describes. Designs are "
      },
      {
        "text": "built from reusable parts",
        "href": "/demo-dc/concepts#composable-topologies"
      },
      {
        "text": ", such as device templates and address pools, so a new data center reuses the same standards. From the generated data, Infrahub renders "
      },
      {
        "text": "device configurations, a cabling plan and a Containerlab topology",
        "href": "/demo-dc/user-walkthrough#step-7-review-validations-and-artifacts"
      },
      {
        "text": " as artifacts."
      }
    ]
  }
]} />

![When you submit the Create DC form in the service portal, the portal creates a branch and, on it, a TopologyDataCenter, dc-arista in this example, with the strategy ospf-ibgp. It references the DesignTopology PHYSICAL DC ARISTA S, which contains 2 spines, 4 leaf switches, 2 firewalls, 2 OOB switches and 2 console servers. On the branch, the Generator creates these 12 devices and connects each spine to each leaf switch. It creates the building dc-arista with Pod-1, Row-1 and one rack per leaf switch: Rack-1 and Rack-2 each hold a leaf switch, a spine, a console server and an OOB switch, and Rack-3 and Rack-4 each hold a leaf switch. The two firewalls are in the building, not in a rack.](./img/demo-dc.svg)

![When you submit the Create VPN form in the service portal, the portal creates a branch and, on it, a ServiceNetworkSegment, web-tier in this example, with the VLAN ID 100, the deployment dc-arista and the segment type l2_only, one of the three segment types l2_only, l3_gateway and l3_vrf. The Generator links each segment to Ethernet1 to Ethernet48 on each of the four leaf switches, 192 interfaces. The example has three segments: web-tier with VLAN 100 and the type l2_only, dmz with VLAN 200 and the type l3_gateway, and database with VLAN 300 and the type l3_vrf. In the configuration of each leaf switch, each segment adds its VLAN, the VLAN on the customer ports, a VXLAN mapping of the VLAN to a VNI, here 10100, 10200 and 10300, and a BGP EVPN block with its route distinguisher and route target. A segment of the type l3_gateway or l3_vrf with a prefix also adds a gateway interface on the first address of the prefix: database, with the prefix 172.25.9.0/24, adds the interface Vlan300 with the virtual address 172.25.9.1/24. dmz has no prefix, so it adds no gateway.](./img/demo-dc-try.svg)
